title: Cell culture and neuronal differentiation
description: Neural stem cells Cor3-1 were cultured in complete media with supplements and growth factors. For neuronal differentiation, cells were transferred to priming medium with B-27 without vitamin A and N2 supplement, followed by differentiation medium with Neurobasal, BDNF, FGF, and Laminin with medium changes every 3 days.
goal: to culture and differentiate neural stem cells into neurons

title: Huwe1 knock-out via adenovirus transduction
description: Neural stem cells with floxed Huwe1-RYFP were transduced with adenovirus CMV-CRE at MOI 100 to induce Huwe1 knock-out. Control cells were transduced with empty adenovirus at the same MOI.
goal: to knock out Huwe1 gene in neural stem cells

title: P19 cell culture and differentiation
description: P19 cells were maintained in MEM-α with FBS and antibiotics. For differentiation, cells were transferred to Neurobasal medium supplemented with B-27 without vitamin A, GlutaMAX, Laminin, and antibiotics with medium changes every 24 hours.
goal: to culture and differentiate P19 cells

title: P19 cell transfection with Lipofectamine 2000
description: P19 cells at 80% confluence were transfected with plasmid DNA using Lipofectamine 2000 at a 1:2 DNA to Lipofectamine ratio in proliferation medium following manufacturer’s instructions.
goal: to transfect P19 cells with plasmid DNA

title: Quantitative Real-Time PCR
description: Total RNA was extracted and reverse transcribed to cDNA. qRT-PCR was performed using SYBR Green Master Mix with EiF1α as housekeeping gene. Thermal cycling conditions included initial denaturation and 40 cycles of amplification.
goal: to quantify gene expression levels

title: Western blotting
description: Proteins were extracted from cells, quantified, separated by SDS-PAGE, and transferred to membranes. Membranes were blocked, incubated with primary and secondary antibodies, and developed using ECL reagents. Experiments were performed in triplicate.
goal: to detect specific proteins by immunoblotting
key_materials: primary antibodies (Ascl1, Histone H3, α-Tubulin, LaminB, Huwe1)

title: Cellular fractionation
description: Cells were washed, pelleted, and sequentially lysed with buffers E1, E2, and E3 to separate cytoplasm, nucleus, and chromatin fractions. Chromatin fraction was sonicated or digested with Benzonase. Fractions were centrifuged and protein concentration determined.
goal: to separate cellular components into cytoplasmic, nuclear, and chromatin fractions

title: Agarose-TUBEs pull down of ubiquitylated proteins
description: Agarose-TUBEs were used to pull down ubiquitylated proteins from cytoplasm and chromatin fractions. After incubation and washing, bound proteins were eluted by boiling in reducing sample buffer and analyzed by SDS-PAGE.
goal: to isolate ubiquitylated proteins from cell fractions

title: Ethics approval for human specimen use
description: Obtained ethics approval in 2020 from the Ethics Reviewing Board of the University Hospital of Liege, Belgium (ref. 2020/119) for the use of human specimens.
goal: to approve the use of human specimens for research

title: Collection and selection of human biopsies
description: Collected lung postmortem biopsy specimens from COVID-19 and non-COVID-19 patients, and additional organ biopsies from COVID-19 patients. Tissues were selected by two pathologists after H&E staining.
goal: to obtain and select human tissue samples for analysis
key_materials: Biobank of the Liege University Hospital

title: Retrospective hematology and biochemistry analysis
description: Analyzed hematology and blood biochemistry retrospectively using the last available blood sample taken within 24 hours before patient death.
goal: to analyze hematology and biochemistry of COVID-19 patients
key_materials: central laboratory (Hematology and Biochemistry) of the Liege University Hospital

title: Histopathological characterization of lung tissues
description: Prepared FFPE lung tissue sections, stained with H&E, digitized whole slides, and assessed high-resolution images focused on NET areas using a scoring system for SARS-CoV-2 diffuse alveolar damage lesions.
goal: to characterize histopathological lesions in lungs from COVID-19 patients

title: Prepare lung tissue sections for immunofluorescence
description: Lung tissues were formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded (FFPE), cut into 4-µm-thick sections, deparaffinized, rehydrated, boiled in sodium carbonate buffer for antigen retrieval, and permeabilized in PBS with 0.5% Triton X-100.
goal: to prepare lung tissue sections suitable for immunofluorescence staining

title: Block and stain lung sections with primary antibodies
description: Tissue sections were incubated with blocking buffer containing PBS, BSA, and donkey serum for 1 hour at room temperature, then stained with rabbit anti-human citrullinated histone H3 and goat anti-human MPO antibodies diluted in blocking buffer for 1 hour at room temperature.
goal: to label NET markers citrullinated histone H3 and MPO in lung sections
key_materials: rabbit anti-human citrullinated histone H3 antibody

title: Incubate with secondary antibodies and mount samples
description: After washing, samples were incubated with secondary antibodies conjugated to Alexa Fluor dyes and DAPI in blocking buffer for 2 hours in the dark at room temperature, then mounted with ProLong Antifade reagent on glass slides and stored overnight in the dark.
goal: to fluorescently label primary antibodies and preserve samples for microscopy

title: Acquire and analyze fluorescence microscopy images
description: Samples were imaged using confocal microscopy with standard filter sets, and images were processed using ImageJ software. Controls included staining with secondary antibodies only to check for nonspecific fluorescence.
goal: to visualize and analyze NET structures in lung tissue
key_materials: Zeiss LSM 880 Airyscan Elyra S.1 confocal microscope

title: Grow tomato plants under controlled conditions
description: Four-week-old tomato plants were germinated in vermiculite under specific light, temperature, and humidity conditions. Seedlings were irrigated with Hoagland solution or modified nutrient solutions lacking nitrogen and supplemented with different nitrogen sources. pH was adjusted to 6.0.
goal: to grow tomato plants under defined nutrient and environmental conditions

title: Apply PA biosynthesis inhibitors and Putrescine treatments
description: Inhibitor solution containing DFMA and DFMO was applied to pots one week prior to Pst inoculation. Putrescine or mock solution was applied as foliar sprays 48 hours before Pst infection.
goal: to inhibit PA biosynthesis or apply Putrescine before pathogen infection

title: Culture and inoculate Pseudomonas syringae
description: Pst and its coronatine-less strain were grown in KB medium with antibiotics. Bacterial suspensions were prepared and used to dip-inoculate tomato leaves. Disease rate was scored at 72 hours post-inoculation.
goal: to infect tomato plants with Pseudomonas syringae for disease assays

title: Culture and prepare Botrytis cinerea spores
description: B. cinerea was cultured on potato dextrose agar. Spores were collected from 10-15 day old cultures, filtered, quantified, and adjusted to 1×10^6 spores/ml.
goal: to prepare Botrytis cinerea spores for bioassays

title: Measure biomass, chlorophyll content, and photosynthetic rate
description: Plant dry weight was measured after drying. Chlorophyll content was measured using a SPAD meter. Net photosynthetic rate was measured using an infrared gas analyser under controlled light and airflow conditions.
goal: to assess plant biomass, chlorophyll levels, and photosynthesis

title: Determine H2O2 accumulation and perform microscopy
description: Leaves were stained with DAB to detect H2O2 and destained for microscopy analysis. H2O2 was quantified using the xylenol orange method by measuring absorbance at 560 nm.
goal: to detect and quantify hydrogen peroxide accumulation in leaves

title: Analyze gene expression by qRT-PCR
description: RNA was extracted from leaf tissue, treated with DNase, and reverse transcribed to cDNA. qRT-PCR was performed using specific primers and SYBR Green detection. EF1α was used as housekeeping control.
goal: to quantify gene expression changes in tomato leaves

title: Analyze stomatal aperture by microscopy
description: Leaves were inoculated with Pst, and epidermal impressions were made using dental resin and nail polish. Stomatal apertures were imaged by light microscopy and measured using software.
goal: to measure stomatal aperture changes after pathogen inoculation

title: Replace fliG gene with pHluorin(M153R)-fliG allele
description: The fliG gene on the Salmonella chromosome was replaced by a pHluorin(M153R)-fliG allele using the λ Red homologous recombination system as described previously.
goal: to replace the fliG gene with a fluorescently tagged allele

title: Prepare L broth and T broth media
description: L broth was prepared as described before. T broth contained 10 g of Bacto tryptone and 5 g of NaCl per liter. Ampicillin and arabinose were added to media at final concentrations of 100 µg/ml and 0.02% (wt/vol), respectively.
goal: to prepare bacterial growth media

title: Perform DNA manipulations and sequencing
description: DNA manipulations were carried out as described previously. DNA sequencing reactions were performed using BigDye v3.1 according to manufacturer’s instructions and analyzed by a 3130 Genetic Analyzer.
goal: to manipulate and sequence DNA

title: Conduct flagellar protein export assay
description: Salmonella cells were grown in LB to OD600 ~1.0, washed with motility buffer, incubated at 30°C for 1 h, and centrifuged to separate cells and supernatants. Cell pellets were resuspended in SDS loading buffer. Proteins in supernatants were precipitated with 10% trichloroacetic acid, suspended in Tris-SDS loading buffer, heated, and analyzed by SDS-PAGE followed by immunoblotting with anti-FlgD and anti-FliC antibodies.
goal: to assay flagellar protein export

title: Purify pHluorin(M153R) and pHluorin(M153R)-FliG-His proteins
description: pHluorin(M153R) was purified from soluble fractions of BL21(DE3)pLysS carrying pYVM007. pHluorin(M153R)-FliG-His was purified by Ni-NTA affinity chromatography from soluble fractions of BL21(DE3)pLysS carrying pYVM013.
goal: to purify fluorescent proteins for further analysis

title: Fluorescence microscopy of Salmonella cells
description: Salmonella cells expressing various pHluorin fusion proteins were observed using a custom-built fluorescence microscope system with specific excitation filters and a high-speed wavelength switcher. Fluorescent images were captured by an EMCCD camera controlled by MetaMorph software.

title: Determination of cytoplasmic pH using pH imaging system
description: Bulk and local cytoplasmic pH of Salmonella cells expressing pHluorin variants were determined from the fluorescence intensity ratio at 410-nm and 470-nm excitation wavelengths. Images were captured with 1 s exposure and analyzed after background subtraction and smoothing to calculate pH using a standard curve from purified proteins.
goal: to determine cytoplasmic pH in Salmonella cells

title: Determination of local pH around export apparatus
description: Fluorescence images with 5 s exposure were used to measure the fluorescence intensity of single pHluorin(M153R)-FliG spots after background subtraction. Local pH was calculated from the 410/470 nm excitation ratio using calibration curves from purified protein and in vivo calibration with treated Salmonella cells.
goal: to determine local pH around the export apparatus

title: Culture primary human astrocytes
description: Primary human astrocytes were expanded in Human Astrocyte Media supplemented with FBS, penicillin streptomycin, and Astrocyte Growth Supplement. Prior to experiments, astrocytes were cultured in a 50:50 mix of F10:MEMα media supplemented with 10% FBS and 1% penicillin streptomycin.

title: Reduce IGF1R levels in astrocytes
description: Astrocytes were treated with 11 μg/ml MAB391 for 24 hours to reduce IGF1R levels. After treatment, cells were washed with PBS and cultured for a further 72 hours in fresh media. An IgG isotype control was included.
goal: to reduce IGF1R levels in astrocytes

title: Culture and differentiate LUHMES cells
description: LUHMES cells were grown in proliferation medium containing DMEM/F12 GlutaMAX™, N2 supplement, and FGF. At 50–60% confluence, cells were differentiated by replacing media with differentiation media containing tetracycline. After two days, cells were trypsinized and replated for an additional three days to become fully differentiated.

title: Generate GFP LUHMES cells
description: Non-differentiated LUHMES cells were transduced with LV-GFP for 24 hours. Media were then replaced with fresh proliferation media and cells were cultured for 72 hours before experiments.

title: Culture fibroblasts as control cells
description: Fibroblasts were cultured in Minimum essential medium supplemented with 10% FBS, 1% penicillin streptomycin, 1% MEM non-essential amino acids, 1% MEM vitamins, 1% sodium pyruvate, and 60 μg/ml uridine. They were used as controls to ensure neurite outgrowth effects were specific to astrocytes.

title: Set up astrocyte-LUHMES co-cultures
description: Astrocytes were seeded onto fibronectin-coated plates and LUHMES were differentiated separately. After two days, LUHMES were replated onto astrocytes and co-cultured for 24 hours in differentiation media. Additional experiments used astrocyte conditioned media and neuron-astrocyte conditioned media to assess contact-mediated support.

title: Set up fibroblast-LUHMES co-cultures
description: Fibroblasts were seeded onto fibronectin-coated plates at a higher density than astrocytes and co-cultured with LUHMES similarly to astrocyte co-cultures.

title: Co-culture with MAB391-treated astrocytes
description: Astrocytes were seeded and treated with MAB391 or MAB002 for 24 hours. GFP LUHMES were then replated onto treated astrocytes with antibody removal. Co-cultures were maintained for 72 hours before treatment with 50 μM H2O2 for 2 hours.

title: In vitro expansion of CD8+CD28− T cells
description: Enriched A-CD8+ T cells were stimulated with B-APCs in the presence of IL-2, IL-7, and IL-15 in 24-well plates for 9 days to generate in vitro-expanded CD8+CD28− T cells.
goal: to generate in vitro-expanded CD8+CD28− T cells

title: CFSE proliferation assay of CD4+ T cells with suppressor cells
description: CFSE-labeled A-CD4+ T cells were cocultured with B-APCs or I-APCs in the presence or absence of in vitro-expanded CD8+CD28− T cells for 7 and 11 days. Proliferation of CD4+ T cells was assessed by CFSE dilution assay.
goal: to assess suppressive capacity of CD8+CD28− T cells on CD4+ T cell proliferation

title: In vivo suppression assay in NOG mice
description: A mixture of human cells including APCs and CD8+CD28− T cells was administered intraperitoneally into NOG mice. After 11 days, spleens were analyzed by flow cytometry and immunohistochemistry to evaluate human CD4+ T cell proliferation and infiltration.
goal: to investigate in vivo suppressive activity of CD8+CD28− T cells

title: Proliferation analysis of CD8+ T cell subsets with cytokines
description: The proliferative capacity of CD8+CD28+ and CD8+CD28− T cells was measured by CFSE dilution after stimulation with APCs in the presence of common gamma chain cytokines for 9 days.
goal: to evaluate proliferation of CD8+ T cell subsets in response to cytokines
key_materials: common gamma chain cytokines (IL-2, IL-7, IL-15)

title: Conversion assay of CD8+CD28+ to CD8+CD28− T cells
description: Purified CD8+CD28+ T cells were cultured with common gamma chain cytokines to observe the generation of CD8+CD28− T cells over time.
goal: to determine if cytokines promote CD28 downregulation on CD8+ T cells
key_materials: common gamma chain cytokines (IL-2, IL-7, IL-15)

title: Annexin V staining for cell survival analysis
description: Cell death rates of CD8+CD28+ and CD8+CD28− T cells were assessed by Annexin V staining after 9 days incubation with or without common gamma chain cytokines.
goal: to evaluate effect of cytokines on survival of CD8+ T cell subsets
key_materials: common gamma chain cytokines (IL-2, IL-7, IL-15)

title: Phenotypic analysis of cytokine receptor expression
description: Expression levels of cytokine receptors CD215, CD122, CD25, and CD132 were compared between freshly purified and in vitro-expanded CD8+CD28− T cells.
goal: to characterize cytokine receptor expression changes after expansion
key_materials: Antibodies for CD215, CD122, CD25, CD132

title: Phenotypic marker analysis of CD8+CD28− T cell subsets
description: Surface and intracellular markers related to differentiation, memory, immunomodulation, and cytotoxicity were analyzed on freshly isolated and expanded CD8+CD28− T cells.
goal: to define phenotypic heterogeneity and functional markers of CD8+CD28− T cells
key_materials: Antibodies for CD27, CD44, CCR7, PD-1, PD-L1, Tim-3, GITR, Granzyme B, Fas ligand

title: Plant growth and preparation for inoculation
description: Seeds of various Phaseolus vulgaris genotypes were sown in vermiculite and grown in a growth chamber at 23°C with a 16 h light/8 h dark cycle and 75% humidity. Seedlings were cultivated for 10-12 days until primary leaves fully expanded, then transplanted into larger pots and placed in a dark room 24 h prior to inoculation.
goal: to grow and prepare plants for viral inoculation

title: Genetic mapping population preparation
description: A population of 77 F11 recombinant inbred lines derived from a cross between JaloEEP558 and BAT93 was grown to the fully-expanded primary leaf stage, placed individually in a dark room 24 h prior to inoculation, and phenotyped 7 days post-inoculation.
goal: to map the R-BPMV resistance gene

title: Construction of BPMV-derived viral vectors
description: RNA2-derived plasmids were constructed by inserting P. vulgaris target gene fragments into the BamH1 site of pBPMV-IA-V1. Target fragments were PCR-amplified using specific primers and high fidelity polymerase, digested with BamH1, and ligated into BamH1-digested and dephosphorylated pBPMV-IA-V1. Insert orientation was verified by PCR and sequencing for antisense clones used in gene silencing.
goal: to generate viral vectors for gene silencing

title: Preparation of viral inoculum and inoculation
description: For primary inoculation, a 20 μL DNA plasmid mix was prepared in mock buffer. For secondary inoculations, infected leaf tissue was ground in mock buffer to prepare leaf sap. Inoculations were performed by mechanical rubbing of one primary leaf. Plants were placed in the dark 24 h prior to inoculation and grown at 19°C under a 16 h light/8 h dark cycle post-inoculation.
goal: to inoculate plants with BPMV viral constructs
key_materials: 50 mM potassium phosphate buffer pH 7.0 (mock buffer)

title: Optimization of rub-inoculation conditions
description: Different DNA plasmid amounts (1.5, 3, or 5 μg each) and rubbing intensities (low, medium, high) were tested on P. vulgaris cv. Black Valentine plants at the fully-expanded primary leaf stage to optimize rub-inoculation efficiency.
goal: to optimize rub-inoculation parameters for BPMV plasmids

title: GFP expression imaging
description: GFP expression in aerial organs and roots was examined under UV light and photographed. Root microscopic observations were performed at 21 days post-inoculation using a microscope and camera.
goal: to visualize GFP expression in inoculated plants

title: Semi-quantitative RT-PCR expression analysis
description: Total RNA was extracted and reverse transcribed to cDNA. PCR amplification was performed using primers targeting PvPDS outside the silencing region and PvUBI as an internal control. PCR products were analyzed by agarose gel electrophoresis after 25 cycles.
goal: to analyze gene expression levels by RT-PCR

title: Genetic mapping of R-BPMV gene
description: Segregation ratios were tested by Chi-squared analysis. The R-BPMV resistance gene was mapped on the integrated linkage map of common bean using MAPMAKER software with a LOD threshold of 3.0 for linkage groups and 2.0 for gene position estimation. Map distances were calculated using the Kosambi function.
goal: to map the R-BPMV resistance gene location

title: Obtain Patient Blood Samples
description: Collected 166 blood samples from 41 patients admitted to Prince of Wales Hospital, Hong Kong, between March and May 2003. Patients met WHO criteria for probable SARS cases, with samples covering acute, convalescent, and recovered phases.

title: Test Patient Samples by RT-PCR
description: Tested samples from 7 patients for SARS-CoV by reverse transcription–polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR) as described in a previous study.
goal: to detect SARS-CoV RNA in patient samples

title: Culture Cell Lines
description: Cultured all cell lines in DMEM supplemented with 10% fetal calf serum and penicillin/streptomycin.
key_materials: DMEM with Glutamax and high glucose

title: Construct QT6/ACE2 Cell Line
description: Cloned human ACE2 gene from kidney cDNA library, subcloned into pcdna3.1+, transfected QT6 cells using lipofectamine 2000, and selected G418-resistant ACE2-positive cells.
goal: to generate QT6 cells expressing human ACE2 receptor

title: Produce Viral Vectors in 293T Cells
description: Transfected 293T cells with gag/pol, GFP reporter, and envelope constructs using Fugene-6. Harvested supernatant at 48 and 72 hours, filtered, and stored at -80°C.
goal: to produce MLV and HIV viral vectors

title: Measure Viral Vector Titer by FACS
description: Infected target cells with viral vectors and determined eGFP titers 72 hours later by fluorescence-activated cell sorting (FACS).
goal: to quantify infectious units of viral vectors

title: Perform Live Virus Neutralization Assay
description: Heat-inactivated patient sera were serially diluted and incubated with 50 PFU SARS virus for 1 hour at 37°C. Added Vero E6 cells and incubated for 4 days. Neutralization assessed by cytopathic effect; endpoint was last well with complete neutralization.
goal: to assess neutralizing antibody activity against live SARS-CoV

title: Perform Pseudotype Neutralization Assay
description: Heat-inactivated patient sera were 2-fold serially diluted and mixed with MLV(SARS) virions. After 1 hour incubation at 37°C, mixtures were added to QT6/ACE2 cells. GFP-positive cells were counted 48 hours later by fluorescence microscopy.
goal: to measure neutralizing antibody titers using pseudotyped virus

title: Analyze growth defects in stn1 mutants
description: Phenotypic categories of stn1 mutants were assessed across generations to quantify developmental defects and correlate them with telomere length.
goal: to quantitatively describe the occurrence of growth defects in stn1 mutants

title: Assess EXO1 effect on STN1-null telomeres
description: Developmental defects, fertility, and genome instability were compared between stn1 and exo1 stn1 mutants to evaluate the role of EXO1 in telomere processing.
goal: to assess the effect of EXO1 on STN1-null telomeres

title: Measure telomere length and G-overhang size
description: Telomere length and single-stranded G-overhangs were quantified in stn1 and exo1 stn1 mutants to determine the contribution of EXO1 to telomere resection.

title: Quantify telomeric permutation frequencies
description: The frequency of telomeric terminal sequence permutations was analyzed in stn1 and exo1 stn1 mutants to detect EXO1-dependent sequence alterations.
goal: to examine whether sequence alteration in STN1-depleted plants is caused by EXO1

title: Generate telomerase-null stn1 mutants
description: Telomerase-null mutants were created to study the contribution of telomerase to G-overhang extension and telomere maintenance in stn1 backgrounds.

title: Perform in gel hybridization for G-overhangs
description: G-overhang sizes were measured in telomerase-null and telomerase-proficient stn1 and exo1 stn1 plants to assess telomerase's role in G-strand extension.

title: Analyze DNA polymerase α mutant phenotypes
description: Growth defects and developmental abnormalities in DNA polymerase α hypomorphic mutants were compared to stn1 mutants to evaluate phenotypic similarities.

title: Detect anaphase bridges in polymerase α mutants
description: Cytogenetic analysis was performed to identify anaphase bridges indicating genome instability in DNA polymerase α mutants.

title: Analyze MCU and related protein mRNA levels
description: Collected mRNA levels of MCU and related proteins (MCUb, MICU1-3, EMRE) from the TCGA breast cancer dataset and analyzed their correlation with tumor size and lymph node infiltration.
goal: to decipher the role of mitochondrial Ca2+ signaling in metastatic potential

title: Measure mitochondrial Ca2+ uptake after MCU silencing
description: Used siRNA to inhibit MCU in three TNBC cell lines and measured agonist-induced mitochondrial Ca2+ uptake using ATP or histamine as agonists.
goal: to verify the hypothesis that mitochondrial Ca2+ uptake affects metastasis

title: Assess cell motility via wound healing assay
description: Monitored cell motility in MCU-silenced TNBC cell lines using wound healing migration assay to evaluate the effect of MCU silencing on migration.
goal: to assess the impact of MCU silencing on cell motility

title: Measure cytosolic Ca2+ transients, SOCE, and ER Ca2+ content
description: Measured cytosolic Ca2+ transients, store-operated Ca2+ entry (SOCE), and ER Ca2+ content in MCU-silenced TNBC cell lines to determine effects on global Ca2+ signaling.
goal: to clarify whether migration impairment is due to reduced mitochondrial Ca2+ uptake or other Ca2+ signaling changes

title: Overexpress MCU and measure mitochondrial Ca2+ uptake
description: Overexpressed MCU in TNBC cell lines and measured agonist-induced mitochondrial Ca2+ uptake and cytosolic Ca2+ transients to assess mitochondrial buffering capacity.

title: Rescue MCU silencing with mouse MCU re-expression
description: Re-expressed mouse MCU in MCU-silenced MDA-MB-231 cells and measured cell motility to confirm specificity of MCU silencing effects.

title: Perform in vitro spheroid invasion assay
description: Generated stable MCU-silenced cells, formed spheroids in agar medium, transferred them to collagen matrix, and monitored radial invasion over time.
goal: to investigate the effect of MCU silencing on cell invasiveness

title: Conduct colony formation assay
description: Assessed cell growth over 7 days in MCU-silenced cells to evaluate proliferation effects.

title: Stain planarian cells with Hoechst and MTG
description: Planarian cell suspension was stained with Hoechst 33342 to identify nuclear content and MTG to measure mitochondrial mass, allowing distinction of X1, X2, and Xins cell populations.
goal: to measure mitochondrial mass in different planarian cell populations

title: Treat cells with Verapamil and stain with MTG
description: Cells were treated with Verapamil, an efflux pump inhibitor, and then stained with MTG to test if low MTG intensity in X1 and X2 cells was due to dye efflux.
goal: to test whether low MTG intensity is due to dye efflux

title: Generate and characterize PIWI-1 antibody
description: An antibody against PIWI-1 was generated and characterized to identify stem cells in planaria by immunostaining, distinguishing PIWI-1 High, Low, and negative cells.
goal: to detect PIWI-1 protein expression in planarian cells

title: Immunostain X1 cells for PIWI-1 expression
description: X1 cells were immunostained with PIWI-1 antibody to compare PIWI-1 expression levels between MTG Low and MTG High subpopulations within X1 cells.
goal: to examine PIWI-1 expression in MTG Low and High X1 cells

title: Perform RNA sequencing on X1-MTG Low and High cells
description: RNA-seq was performed on X1 cells sorted by low and high MTG fluorescence to identify differentially expressed genes and characterize neoblast heterogeneity.
goal: to understand functional states of X1-MTG Low and High cells

title: Immunostain X2-MTG Low and High cells for PIWI-1
description: X2 cells sorted by MTG fluorescence were immunostained for PIWI-1 to assess stem cell marker expression in MTG Low and High subpopulations.
goal: to investigate stem state of MTG Low and High X2 cells

title: Sort X2-MTG Low and High cells by size (FSC)
description: X2-MTG Low and High cells were further sorted based on forward scatter (FSC) to separate high and low size cells, resulting in four populations for further analysis.
goal: to separate PIWI-1 High and Low cells within X2-MTG populations

title: Perform RNA sequencing on X2-MTG Low and High populations
description: RNA-seq was conducted on combined high and low FSC X2-MTG Low and High populations to analyze gene expression profiles related to stemness and differentiation.
goal: to characterize transcriptomic differences in X2-MTG Low and High cells

title: Generate fluorescence reporter mice
description: Crossed Pax2-Cre mice with R26R-Lyn-Venus mice to produce fluorescence reporter mice for live-imaging analysis.
goal: to produce fluorescence reporter mice for live-imaging analysis

title: Sacrifice mice at embryonic stages
description: Sacrificed mice by cervical dislocation at embryonic day 15.5 or 16.5 to minimize suffering.

title: Immunostaining with primary antibodies
description: Used various primary antibodies at 1:200 dilution for immunostaining with appropriate fixatives (PFA or TCA) depending on the target epitope.

title: Whole-tissue immunofluorescence staining
description: Fixed dissected epididymides, blocked with normal serum, incubated with primary antibodies overnight at 4°C, followed by secondary antibodies conjugated to Alexa Fluor dyes. Used phalloidin and Hoechst for F-actin and DNA visualization.
key_materials: 2% TCA in Ca2+- and Mg2+-free PBS

title: Volumetric fluorescence imaging
description: Mounted samples in agarose gel, optically cleared with BABB or CUBIC2, and acquired 8-bit volumetric fluorescence images using confocal microscopy with various objective lenses.

title: Explant organ culture of epididymides
description: Dissected epididymides with testis, placed on culture inserts in Petri dishes with culture medium, and cultured at 37°C under 5% CO2 in an air-liquid interface.

title: Treatment with small-molecule inhibitors
description: Applied specific inhibitors to samples during culture to modulate cellular processes.

title: Live imaging of cultured epididymides
description: Prepared organ culture inserts adhered with agarose gel to prevent sliding, and performed live imaging using multiphoton microscopy with specified imaging parameters.

title: Scan maize CoREGs for acetyl-CoA-binding site
description: Each cloned HAG maize CoREG was scanned for the presence of an acetyl-CoA-binding site using the Conserved Domain Database. This region of approximately 75–90 amino acids was identified for further analysis.
goal: to identify acetyl-CoA-binding sites in maize CoREGs

title: Perform phylogenetic analysis of CoREG proteins
description: Related proteins were aligned using Clustal W with default parameters via the megalign program. For AUX/IAA CoREGs, full-length amino acid sequences were aligned using MUSCLE with specified parameters. Multiple sequence alignments were exported in Newick format and phylogenetic trees were displayed using FigTree.
goal: to perform phylogenetic analysis of maize CoREG proteins

title: Clone TF and CoREG ORFs into pENTR vectors
description: Targeted TF or CoREG open reading frames were amplified using high-fidelity Phusion polymerase with GC buffer supplemented with 10% glycerol. Optimization included addition of up to 10% DMSO, up to 4 mM MgCl2, or annealing temperature adjustments. Primers were designed without stop codons and with a 5′-CACC tail for directional cloning into pENTR vectors.
goal: to clone TF and CoREG ORFs into entry vectors

title: Screen and confirm cloned inserts
description: Kanamycin-resistant colonies were screened for correct insert size and orientation by colony PCR or restriction digestion. Cloned inserts were confirmed by single-read paired-end Sanger sequencing. For inserts longer than 1200 bp, internal primers were used to complete sequence confirmation.
goal: to verify correct cloning of TF and CoREG inserts

title: Clone ORFs into pENTR vectors
description: Targeted transcription factor or CoREG ORFs were amplified using high-fidelity Phusion polymerase with GC buffer and additives like glycerol, DMSO, or MgCl2. Primers were designed without stop codons and with a 5′-CACC tail for directional cloning into pENTR vectors. Kanamycin-resistant colonies were screened by colony PCR or restriction digestion, and inserts were sequence confirmed by Sanger sequencing.
goal: to clone ORFs into pENTR vectors for further use

title: Grow maize plants and isolate DNA/RNA
description: B73 maize plants were grown in a field nursery. Genomic DNA was isolated using a CTAB-based method. Total RNA was isolated from non-starchy tissues using RNAzol and from starchy tissues using a modified Li and Trick protocol. RNA integrity was verified by agarose gel electrophoresis and ethidium bromide staining.
goal: to isolate genomic DNA and total RNA from maize tissues

title: Test codon optimization of synthesized ORFs
description: Synthesized coding sequences optimized for maize, yeast, or hybrid codon usage were recombined into GAL4-BD-GWC1 vector for yeast expression and into p1511 plasmid for GFP fusion under the 35S promoter to test expression in maize protoplasts.
goal: to determine codon optimization strategy for synthesized ORFs

title: Transform yeast cells and perform Western blot
description: Yeast cells were transformed with GAL4-BD-GWC1 constructs using the lithium acetate method. Cells were grown to OD600=0.6, lysed with NaOH, and proteins were prepared in SDS loading buffer. Samples were analyzed by 10% SDS-PAGE and Western blot using specific primary and secondary antibodies. Exposure times varied depending on the gene clone.
goal: to verify protein expression of codon-optimized constructs in yeast

title: Design probes from input sequences
description: Generate variable length probes (50-100 mers) from 300,919 input sequences derived from gene models, full-length cDNA, and de novo assembled RNA-Seq contigs. Repeat-mask probes by removing those with high 15-mer frequency and eliminate probes with more than 25 matches in the target set. Select 2,040,943 unique probes spaced on average 40 bp apart for array design.
goal: to design a probe set for hybridization

title: Hybridize array with barley cultivars
description: Hybridize two slides of the array design with four barley cultivars using standard comparative genomic hybridization (CGH) protocols for 4 days. Remove probes with high signal intensity or low signal across all cultivars to exclude repetitive elements and contaminants.
goal: to validate and optimize probe performance
key_materials: barley cultivars Steptoe, Barke, Morex, Bowman

title: Prepare Illumina TruSeq paired-end libraries
description: Fragment 1 μg genomic DNA to 200-300 bp using Covaris S220. Optionally size fractionate adapter-ligated products to 320-420 bp by gel excision. Purify libraries with AmPure XP beads and elute in resuspension buffer.
goal: to prepare sequencing libraries for capture
key_materials: Illumina TruSeq Paired End library kit

title: Pre-capture LM-PCR amplification
description: Enrich correctly ligated DNA fragments by ligation-mediated PCR using Illumina sequencing adapters and Phusion polymerase. Quantify and analyze amplified libraries electrophoretically to confirm fragment size between 250-500 bp.
goal: to enrich and amplify sequencing libraries before capture

title: Prepare capture library with blocking oligos
description: Add PCE and blocking oligos to amplified libraries, dry down, then add hybridization buffer and component. Denature and incubate with liquid array for hybridization at 47°C for 64-72 hours.
goal: to prepare libraries for hybridization-based capture

title: Wash and purify captured DNA with Dynabeads
description: Prepare Dynabeads by washing and resuspending in bead wash buffer. Bind hybridized sample to beads at 47°C for 45 min with intermittent vortexing. Perform sequential washes with SC Wash Buffer I, Stringent Wash Buffer, and Wash Buffers I-III at specified temperatures. Resuspend bead-bound captured library in PCR-grade water.
goal: to purify captured DNA from hybridization mixture

title: Amplify captured library by LM-PCR
description: Amplify bead-bound captured library using LM-PCR with Illumina adapters and Phusion polymerase under specified cycling conditions. Combine reactions and purify PCR products using Qiaquick columns with modified washing and elution steps. Assess DNA purity and fragment size by spectrophotometry and bioanalyzer.
goal: to enrich captured DNA for sequencing

title: Map target regions and analyze sequencing data
description: Map target transcript contigs to barley Morex genome assembly using BWA and Mega BLAST. Map sequencing reads to assembly and compute coverage with SAMtools. Perform coverage statistics and regression analysis in R. Identify off-target high coverage regions and filter BLAST results. Call SNPs using SAMtools mpileup/BCFtools and filter with custom scripts.
goal: to analyze exome sequencing data and identify variants

title: Culture D. coniospora and extract genomic DNA
description: D. coniospora strain ATCC 96282 was cultured at 25°C on solid NGM with C. elegans or in liquid NGMY medium without nematodes. After 7 days, mycelia were harvested by vacuum filtering, dried, ground in liquid nitrogen, and DNA was extracted using the DNeasy Plant Mini Kit.
goal: to extract fungal genomic DNA

title: Prepare samples and extract RNA from spores and mycelia
description: Fresh spores were collected and inoculated in NGMY liquid medium, cultured for 4 days or serially cultured. Samples were filtered, flash frozen, and stored at -80°C. Aliquots were homogenized in Trizol and RNA was purified and cleaned with RNeasy mini Kit.
goal: to prepare RNA samples from spores and mycelia

title: Construct genomic DNA libraries and perform sequencing
description: MIseq paired-end libraries were prepared from genomic DNA and sequenced as 2 x 150 bp reads. For SOLiD sequencing, mate-paired libraries were prepared, DNA sheared to 1.5 kb or 3 kb fragments, nick-translated, PCR amplified, size-selected, purified, and sequenced on the 5500 WildFire system.
goal: to generate genomic DNA sequence data
key_materials: SOLiD Library Micro Column Purification Kit

title: Construct cDNA libraries and perform Illumina sequencing
description: cDNA libraries were constructed from mRNA of spores and mycelia and sequenced using Illumina HiSeq 2000, yielding over 48 million 90 bp paired-end reads per library.
goal: to sequence mRNA from spores and mycelia

title: Perform de novo genome assembly
description: MIseq reads were filtered for quality and contaminants using BBDuk. Filtered reads were assembled de novo using Velvet, SPAdes, SOAPdenovo2, and ABySS. Resulting assemblies were scaffolded using high-quality SOLiD mate-paired reads with SSPACE.
goal: to assemble the D. coniospora genome

title: Perform de novo transcriptome assembly
description: Combined reads from spores and mycelia libraries were assembled de novo into a transcriptome using Trinity with default parameters.
goal: to assemble the transcriptome for gene prediction

title: Generate optical genome map
description: A whole genome map was generated using the Argus system with XbaI enzyme selected for optimal fragment sizes. Molecules longer than 200 kb were assembled with MapSolver, manually validated, and used for comparison with in silico digestion profiles.
goal: to create a physical genome map for validation

title: Annotate repetitive elements and non-coding RNAs
description: Repetitive elements were identified using RepeatScout and masked with RepeatMasker. Transposable elements were characterized with TransposonPSI. Non-coding RNAs were identified using Rfam scan and tRNAscan-SE.
goal: to annotate repetitive and non-coding genomic elements

title: siRNA Screen Setup and Infection
description: siRNA SMARTpools were dispensed into 384-well plates and stored at -80°C. On the day of transfection, plates were thawed, transfection reagent added, and complexes formed. Hela cells were trypsinised, counted, and added to wells. After 48 h incubation, cells were infected with HSV-1-eGFP virus or media, incubated, and virus replication monitored by eGFP fluorescence.
goal: to perform siRNA knockdown and measure HSV-1 replication

title: Cell Viability Assay Using CellTiter Blue
description: After siRNA transfection, CellTiter Blue reagent was added to wells and incubated for 2 h. Fluorescence was measured to assess cell viability relative to mock-transfected controls. Viability below 60% was considered cytotoxic.
goal: to determine cytotoxicity of siRNAs

title: Yeast Two-Hybrid Protein Interaction Screen
description: HSV-1 clones were cloned into bait vectors and screened against a prey library using a semi-automated yeast two-hybrid assay. Interacting prey cDNAs were identified by database blasting and a high-confidence dataset was generated from repeated or related interactions.
goal: to identify protein-protein interactions between HSV-1 and human proteins

title: Bioinformatic Analysis of Protein Interactions
description: HSV-1-human protein interactions were integrated with human protein interaction networks. Betweenness centrality was calculated, and enrichment for functional annotations was performed. Protein complexes with consistent effects were identified using statistical tests.
goal: to analyze and interpret protein interaction networks

title: siRNA SMARTpool Deconvolution for Validation
description: Individual siRNAs and reconstituted SMARTpools were diluted and dispensed into plates. Transfection and infection were performed as in the primary screen. Replication slopes were calculated and normalized; validation required at least two siRNAs showing consistent phenotype.
goal: to validate HSV-1 replication phenotypes from primary screen

title: HSV-1 Replication Assay in 96-Well Plates
description: siRNA SMARTpools were dispensed into 96-well plates, transfection reagent added, and complexes formed. Hela cells were seeded and incubated for 48 h before infection with HSV-1. Virus replication was monitored by eGFP fluorescence over time.
goal: to measure HSV-1 replication after siRNA treatment

title: VZV Replication Assay in 384-Well Plates
description: siRNA SMARTpools were dispensed and transfection complexes formed. MeWo cells were seeded and incubated for 48 h before infection with VZV-eGFP-infected cells. Virus growth was measured by eGFP fluorescence at 3 h intervals.
goal: to measure VZV replication after siRNA treatment

title: hCMV Replication Assay in 384-Well Plates
description: siRNA SMARTpools were dispensed and transfection complexes formed. MRC-5 cells were seeded and incubated for 48 h before infection with hCMV-GFP. Virus replication was monitored by eGFP fluorescence from 24 to 80 h post-infection.
goal: to measure hCMV replication after siRNA treatment

title: Confirm viral vector infectivity on embryos
description: Microinject AAV, adenoviral, and lentiviral vectors encoding EGFP into the perivitelline space of pronuclear-stage mouse embryos and confirm EGFP expression at morula/blastocyst stage by fluorescence microscopy.
goal: to confirm infectivity of viral vectors on embryos

title: Co-culture embryos with viral vectors
description: Co-culture embryos with intact zona pellucida with viral vectors and observe infection efficiency by transgene expression.
goal: to test infection efficiency of viral vectors on embryos with intact zona pellucida

title: Test AAV vector infection on parthenogenetic embryos
description: Infect parthenogenetic embryos with AAV vector and confirm infection by transgene expression.
goal: to test if AAV vector can infect embryos without fertilization

title: Evaluate AAV transduction efficiency in rat and bovine embryos
description: Infect rat and bovine embryos with AAV6 vector and assess transduction efficiency.
goal: to evaluate AAV vector suitability for different mammalian species

title: Knockin at mouse Rosa26 locus using scAAV vector
description: Electroporate Cas9-RNP into pronuclear-stage mouse embryos, infect with scAAV vector carrying CAG-GFP cassette flanked by Rosa26 homology arms, and assess knockin efficiency at blastocyst stage and in offspring.
goal: to achieve large-fragment knockin at Rosa26 locus in mouse embryos

title: Knockin at mouse Rosa26 locus using ssAAV vector
description: Electroporate Cas9-RNP into pronuclear-stage mouse embryos, infect with ssAAV vector carrying CAG-GFP cassette flanked by longer Rosa26 homology arms, and assess knockin efficiency and germline transmission.
goal: to achieve large-fragment knockin at Rosa26 locus in mouse embryos

title: Knockin at rat Rosa26 locus using scAAV vector
description: Electroporate Cas9-RNP into pronuclear-stage rat embryos, infect with scAAV vector carrying CAG-GFP cassette flanked by Rosa26 homology arms, and assess knockin efficiency and germline transmission.
goal: to achieve large-fragment knockin at Rosa26 locus in rat embryos

title: Knockin at rat Rosa26 locus using ssAAV vector
description: Electroporate Cas9-RNP into pronuclear-stage rat embryos, infect with ssAAV vector carrying CAG-GFP cassette flanked by longer Rosa26 homology arms, and assess knockin efficiency, mosaicism, and germline transmission.
goal: to achieve large-fragment knockin at Rosa26 locus in rat embryos

title: Cell culture of 293T and 293L cells
description: 293T and 293L cells were grown in DMEM supplemented with bovine growth serum, l-glutamine, penicillin, and streptomycin. 293L cells harboring various BAC16 or BAC36 constructs were cultured with additional hygromycin B for selection.

title: Culture of iSLK and TRExBCBL1-RTA cells
description: iSLK.219 and derivative cells were maintained in DMEM with Tet-Free FBS and antibiotics including hygromycin B, G418, and puromycin. TRExBCBL1-RTA and BCBL-1 cells were grown in RPMI with fetal bovine serum and antibiotics.

title: Generation of lentiviral vectors and transduction
description: Lentiviral vectors expressing ORF59-Flag or dsRed-ORF59-Flag were generated by cloning genes into vectors and transfecting 293T cells with packaging plasmids. Viruses were collected and used to transduce target cells, followed by puromycin selection.

title: Transfection of BAC16 ORF59-Flag into 293L cells
description: BAC16 ORF59-Flag was transfected into 293L cells using Metafectene Pro reagent. Cells were selected with hygromycin to maintain KSHV BACs.

title: Plasmid construction and cloning
description: Various plasmids were generated by PCR amplification and cloning, including full-length and truncated constructs of PRMT5, COPR5, and ORF59. Integrity was confirmed by sequencing.

title: Generation of Flag-tagged ORF59 BACmid by homologous recombination
description: A Flag epitope tag was inserted at the C-terminus of ORF59 in BAC16 by a two-step seamless galK positive/counter selection homologous recombination. Correct insertion was confirmed by restriction digestion, Southern blot, PCR, and sequencing.
goal: to generate a recombinant KSHV BAC16 with ORF59-Flag tagged

title: Antibody usage for detection and immunoprecipitation
description: A panel of antibodies targeting Flag, RTA, LANA, Myc, HA, GFP, GAPDH, PRMT5, ORF59, and controls were used for Western blotting, immunoprecipitation, and chromatin immunoprecipitation assays.

title: Co-immunoprecipitation and Western blotting
description: 293T cells were transfected with expression vectors using PEI. After 48 h, cells were lysed in RIPA buffer with protease inhibitors. Lysates were precleared, incubated with antibodies overnight, and immune complexes captured with Protein A/G beads. Samples were analyzed by SDS-PAGE and Western blot.

title: Antibody selection for ChIP
description: Selected specific antibodies for chromatin immunoprecipitation (ChIP) targeting histone modifications H3K4Me3, H3K9Me3, H3K27Me3, and total H3.

title: Fixation and sorting of Drosophila larval brain cells
description: Dissected larval brains 48 hours post hatching, fixed with 1% formaldehyde for 10 minutes at room temperature, quenched with glycine, dissociated cells, and sorted by GFP intensity and size on BD FACSAria to isolate type II neural stem cells.
goal: to fix and isolate pure type II NSCs from Drosophila larval brains

title: Fixation and sorting of K562 cells
description: Cultured K562 cells were fixed with 1% formaldehyde for 10 minutes at room temperature, crosslink quenched with glycine, stained with Hoechst, and 100 cells were sorted directly into RIPA buffer using BD FACSAria.
goal: to fix and sort K562 cells for downstream analysis
key_materials: RPMI medium with 10% Fetal Bovine Serum

title: Culture and Fix K562 Cells
description: K562 cells were cultured in RPMI medium supplemented with 10% Fetal Bovine Serum at 37°C and 5% CO2. Cells were fixed with 1% formaldehyde for 10 minutes at room temperature, quenched with 125 mM glycine, and sorted using Hoechst stain on a BD FACSAria cell sorter. A total of 100 cells were sorted directly into RIPA 140 mM buffer.

title: Conventional ChIP-Seq Sample Preparation
description: Fixed cells were resuspended in 140 mM RIPA buffer and sonicated for 14 cycles using a bioruptor. After centrifugation, the supernatant was incubated overnight with 2 μg of specific antibody at 4°C. Protein A and G Dynabeads were added to capture antibodies, followed by sequential washes with RIPA buffers and TE buffer. Samples were treated with RNase and Proteinase K to reverse cross-links, then DNA was extracted by phenol–chloroform and dissolved in TE buffer. DNA was converted into sequencing libraries using the NebNext Ultra II kit.
goal: to prepare chromatin immunoprecipitated DNA libraries for sequencing
key_materials: NebNext Ultra II DNA library preparation kit

title: TAF-ChIP Sample Preparation and Library Construction
description: Cells were fixed with 1% formaldehyde and quenched with glycine, washed with PBS, and sorted into RIPA buffer. Cells were sonicated at low power to break nuclei. Protein A and G Dynabeads were coupled with specific antibody in blocking buffer. Chromatin was centrifuged and incubated overnight with antibody-coupled beads. Beads were washed with homemade tagmentation buffer and subjected to tagmentation using Nextera enzyme. After tagmentation, beads were washed with RIPA and TE buffers. Samples underwent Proteinase K treatment overnight at 60°C. DNA was either phenol–chloroform extracted and precipitated or directly PCR-amplified after heat inactivation of Proteinase K. PCR products were purified by bead-based size selection, analyzed for size and concentration, pooled, and sequenced.
goal: to perform TAF-ChIP and prepare sequencing libraries from low cell numbers
key_materials: blocking buffer (RIPA 140 mM + BSA + glycogen + yeast tRNA)

title: PCR purification with bead-based size selection
description: PCR reaction was purified by adding Ampure Xp beads at 0.2× ratio to bind and remove fragments larger than 1,000 bp, followed by magnetic separation and transfer of supernatant. Then, beads were added at 0.8× ratio to bind the target library.
goal: to purify PCR products by removing large fragments and isolating target library

title: Library quality analysis and quantification
description: Purified libraries were analyzed for size distribution using Agilent Bioanalyzer and their concentration was measured using a Qubit fluorometer.
goal: to assess library size distribution and concentration

title: Screen Arabidopsis genes for Chl biosynthesis regulators
description: Screened datasets for Arabidopsis genes of unknown function with transcriptional signatures of CBGs or CCGs to identify novel regulators of chlorophyll biosynthesis and catabolism.
goal: to identify novel regulators of Chl biosynthesis and catabolism

title: Immunoblot analysis of BCM1 protein accumulation
description: Performed immunoblot analyses using BCM1 antiserum to detect BCM1 protein accumulation in various Arabidopsis tissues.

title: Transient expression of BCM1-YFP in protoplasts
description: Transiently expressed BCM1 fused to yellow fluorescent protein in Arabidopsis protoplasts to determine subcellular localization.

title: Subfractionation of chloroplasts and immunoblot analysis
description: Isolated chloroplast subfractions and performed immunoblot analyses to determine BCM1 localization within chloroplast compartments.

title: Chaotropic and alkaline treatment of thylakoids
description: Treated isolated thylakoids with chaotropic and alkaline reagents to assess whether BCM1 is an integral or peripheral membrane protein.

title: Phenotypic and biochemical characterization of bcm1 mutants and BCM1-OX plants
description: Characterized leaf phenotypes, ALA synthesis rates, and chlorophyll and Mg-porphyrin contents in bcm1 mutants and BCM1-overexpressing seedlings under various light conditions.
goal: to investigate the function of BCM1 in Chl biosynthesis

title: Immunoblot and qRT-PCR analyses of CBGs and CBEs
description: Examined expression and protein levels of chlorophyll biosynthesis genes and enzymes in bcm1 mutants and BCM1-OX seedlings to assess post-translational effects.

title: Genetic interaction analysis of bcm1 with gun5 and gun4 mutants
description: Generated double mutants combining bcm1-3 with gun5 and gun4 alleles to study genetic interactions affecting Mg chelatase activity and chlorophyll biosynthesis.

title: Mouse strain preparation and genotyping
description: Various mouse strains including C57BL/6, Tlr7−/−, Tlr9−/−, Myd88−/−, and Tlr7−/− Tlr9−/− double knockout mice were used. All strains were confirmed to have a C57BL/6 background greater than 95% by microsatellite genotyping.

title: Parasite maintenance and infection initiation
description: P. berghei ANKA parasites were maintained in C57BL/6 mice. Blood was harvested by cardiac puncture from infected mice on day 5 post-infection, and 10^6 infected erythrocytes were injected intraperitoneally into new mice in 100 μl of Alsever’s solution. Infections were initiated at 14:00 hours.
goal: to initiate malaria infection in mice

title: Blood collection for cytokine analysis
description: Blood was collected from infected mice by submandibular blood collection or cardiac puncture into K2EDTA tubes for plasma isolation used in cytokine analysis.

title: Monitoring infection progression and cerebral malaria symptoms
description: Survival and signs of cerebral malaria were monitored daily, and twice daily during peak lethality (days 6-12). Parasitaemia was monitored daily by Giemsa-stained thin blood smears. Neurological symptoms such as convulsions, ataxia, or paralysis were recorded to identify cerebral malaria cases.

title: Statistical analysis of parasitaemia and survival
description: The significance of parasitaemia courses was assessed using the Mann–Whitney U test (α=0.05). Survival curves were compared using Kaplan-Meier analysis with the log rank (Mantel-Cox) test (α=0.05).

title: Plasma cytokine measurement by multiplex bead assay
description: Plasma cytokines were measured using a multiplexed cytometric bead immunoassay according to manufacturer instructions and detected on a MAGPIX instrument. Cytokine level significance was assessed using the Mann–Whitney U test (α=0.05).
key_materials: Millipore multiplexed cytometric bead immunoassay kit

title: Treat Satellite Cells with Muscle Extracts
description: Satellite cells associated with myofibers were treated with TA muscle extracts in floating culture conditions. Immunofluorescence was used to assess activation markers PAX7, MYOD, Ki67, and EdU incorporation after 24 hours.
goal: to examine the effect of muscle extracts on satellite cell activation

title: Co-culture Intact and Damaged Myofibers
description: Healthy intact myofibers were co-cultured with mechanically damaged myofibers obtained by pipette damage. Satellite cell activation and proliferation markers were analyzed at 48 and 72 hours to assess the effect of damaged myofiber-derived factors (DMDFs).
goal: to evaluate whether DMDFs directly stimulate satellite cell activation and proliferation

title: Washout and Recovery of Satellite Cells Post-DMDF Stimulation
description: After co-culture with damaged myofibers and DMDF-containing media, the damaged myofibers and media were washed out and replaced with fresh DMEM. Satellite cells were cultured for an additional 24 hours to assess reversibility of activation to a quiescent-like state.
goal: to test whether activated satellite cells in G1 phase revert to quiescence

title: Proteome Analysis to Identify DMDFs
description: Proteins from supernatants of intact and damaged myofiber cultures were analyzed by SDS-PAGE and proteomics to identify candidate DMDF proteins ranging from 10 to 50 kDa.
goal: to identify metabolic enzymes acting as DMDFs that stimulate satellite cell activation

title: Treat Satellite Cells with Recombinant Metabolic Enzymes
description: Isolated myofibers with satellite cells were treated with recombinant metabolic enzymes or controls in floating culture for 72 hours. Immunostaining for MYOD, PAX7, Ki67, and EdU was performed to assess activation and cell cycle entry.
goal: to test if extracellular metabolic enzymes stimulate satellite cell activation independent of glucose metabolism

title: Treat Satellite Cells with Metabolic Enzymes in Non-Glucose Medium
description: Satellite cells associated with myofibers were treated with metabolic enzymes in non-glucose DMEM to exclude glucose metabolism effects. Activation was assessed by PAX7 and MYOD immunostaining.
goal: to determine if metabolic enzyme-induced activation occurs independent of glucose

title: Test c-MET Inhibitor Effect on DMDF-Induced Activation
description: Satellite cells treated with recombinant DMDFs were also treated with the c-MET inhibitor PHA-665752 to assess whether HGF/c-MET signaling is required for DMDF-induced activation.
goal: to determine if HGF signaling is necessary for DMDF-induced satellite cell activation

title: Assess Satellite Cell Activation on Damaged Myofibers
description: Satellite cells associated with damaged (shrunken/dying) myofibers, which lack functional myonuclei, were analyzed for entry into the G1 phase using immunofluorescence. This tested if DMDFs activate satellite cells directly rather than indirectly via intact myofibers.
goal: to test if DMDFs activate satellite cells directly

title: Ethical approval and tissue micro-dissection
description: Ethical approval was obtained. Laser micro-dissection (LMD) was performed on formalin-fixed/paraffin-embedded tissue using a Zeiss/PALM Microscope. SMA staining was performed using a mouse monoclonal antibody and an automated stainer under standard conditions.
goal: to obtain ethically approved tissue samples and isolate specific cell types by laser micro-dissection

title: Cell culture and genetic modification
description: MCF7 and HB2 cells were cultured. Stable GFP expression was introduced using pTH-GFPa vector. MCF7 cells expressing firefly luciferase were obtained. Primary fibroblasts were isolated and immortalized by hTERT retroviral transduction. Reverse transfection of pre-/anti-miR and plasmids was performed using HiPerFect. Stable miR-26b knockdown was achieved using pmiRZIP lentiviral vectors.
goal: to culture and genetically modify cells for functional assays

title: Functional cell assays
description: Assays for cell viability, cell cycle, apoptosis, migration, and invasion were performed. Flow cytometry and fluorescence-activated cell sorting were conducted using LSRII and MoFlo machines. Spheroid invasion assays were performed with modifications. Spheroids were fixed, embedded, sectioned, stained with haematoxylin/eosin or immunohistochemistry with anti-cytokeratin antibody. Dual luciferase assays were performed using pmiRGLO reporter.
goal: to assess cellular functions including viability, migration, invasion, and gene expression

title: RNA extraction and gene expression analysis
description: RNA was extracted from FFPE tissue using RecoverAll kit. miRNA and mRNA were extracted from cell lines using MirVana and RNeasy kits respectively. qPCR analyses were performed in triplicate using Taqman assays on 7500/7900HT machines. Microarray analyses of miRNA expression were performed using human miRNA v2 arrays and system v1.7 reagents.
goal: to extract RNA and analyze gene and miRNA expression
key_materials: RecoverAll Total Nucleic Acid Isolation kit (Ambion)

title: Protein mass spectrometry analysis
description: Peptides from processed cell pellet lysates were separated by capillary liquid chromatography and analyzed by tandem mass spectrometry using RSLCnano and LTQ-Orbitrap Velos instruments. Data were searched against the IPI Human 3.87 database and label-free quantitation was performed using MaxQuant software.
goal: to identify and quantify proteins from cell lysates

title: Statistical data analysis
description: Statistical analyses were performed using Prism with two-tailed tests. Mass spectrometry data were analyzed using R; expression levels were log2 median-normalized and analyzed using t-tests. P values were adjusted to false discovery rates using Benjamini–Hochberg methodology.
goal: to analyze experimental data statistically

title: Compile TDP43 homolog sequence database
description: Collected protein sequences of 93 vertebrate TDP43 homologs and separated them into NTDs, RRM domains, and CTDs for evolutionary sequence analysis.
goal: to decode the sequence rules relating TDP43 phase behavior to amino-acid sequence

title: Calculate sequence diversity by edit distance
description: Calculated the Levenshtein (edit) distance normalized to 100 amino acids between all members of NTD, RRM, and CTD collections to assess sequence diversity.
goal: to measure sequence diversity within TDP43 domain collections

title: Analyze amino-acid composition of TDP43 CTD subdomains
description: Analyzed amino-acid composition of the conserved region (CR) and two intrinsically disordered regions (IDRs) flanking the CR, focusing on residue enrichment and depletion patterns.
goal: to identify conserved higher-order sequence patterns in TDP43 CTD

title: Assess hydrophobic residue spacing in TDP43 IDRs
description: Examined the number, relative position, and spacing of hydrophobic residues in IDRs across vertebrate TDP43 homologs to identify conserved periodic hydrophobic patterns.
goal: to characterize conserved hydrophobic spacing in TDP43 IDRs

title: Calculate hydrophobicity profiles of TDP43 CTD
description: Computed hydrophobicity using a sliding window of five amino acids with fourteen hydrophobicity scales to illustrate periodic hydrophobic motifs in human and vertebrate TDP43 CTDs.
goal: to illustrate conserved periodic hydrophobic patterns in TDP43 CTD

title: Generate TDP43 RRM-GFP phase separation reporter
description: Replaced RNA-binding RRM domains of TDP43 with GFP to create a reporter protein that forms micron-sized liquid droplets suitable for live-cell phase separation analysis.
goal: to rapidly measure TDP43 LLPS in living cells

title: Screen CTD mutants using TDP43 RRM-GFP reporter
description: Used the TDP43 RRM-GFP reporter assay to identify CTD mutations that alter phase separation propensity or properties, focusing on hydrophobic motif composition and spacing.
goal: to identify mutations affecting TDP43 phase separation

title: Mutate hydrophobic residues to serine in TDP43 CTD
description: Created mutants replacing all hydrophobic residues (VLIMFYW) with serine to test their role in phase separation and localization of TDP43 RRM-GFP in cells.
goal: to test the role of hydrophobic residues in TDP43 phase separation

title: Design and clone cDNAs into pBABED-Puro vectors
description: cDNAs encoding various FLAG-tagged proteins and human VHL were designed from published protein sequences and cloned into pBABED-Puro vectors for constitutive expression.
goal: to constitutively express FLAG-tagged proteins and human VHL

title: Verify DNA constructs by sequencing
description: All DNA constructs were verified by DNA sequencing performed by the DNA Sequencing and Services at MRCPPU using Applied Biosystems Big-Dye chemistry and automated sequencer.
goal: to verify the accuracy of DNA constructs
key_materials: Applied Biosystems model 3730 automated capillary DNA sequencer

title: Obtain retroviral expression system vectors
description: Retroviral expression system vectors pCMV-Gag-Pol and pCMV-VSVG were obtained from Clontech, as well as pRetroX-Tet-On and pRetroX-Tight vectors for inducible AdPROM expression.

title: Obtain siRNAs for control and SHP2 knockdown
description: Non-targeting control siRNAs and SHP2 siRNA pool were obtained from Dharmacon for use in gene silencing experiments.

title: Culture human and mouse cell lines
description: Human U2OS, A549, MDA-MB-468, MDA-MB-231, K-562 and mouse J774 cells were cultured in DMEM or RPMI supplemented with FBS, l-glutamine, and penicillin/streptomycin at 37°C with 5% CO2.

title: Produce retroviruses by co-transfection in 293-FT cells
description: pBABED retroviral plasmids were co-transfected with pCMV-gag-pol and pCMV-VSV-G into 293-FT cells using PEI in Opti-MEM medium. After incubation, retroviral particles were collected and filtered.
goal: to produce retroviral particles for infection

title: Infect target cells with retroviral medium and select
description: Target cells at ~60% confluence were infected with retroviral medium containing polybrene for 24 h, then selected with puromycin to enrich for cells with integrated retrovirus.
goal: to generate stable cell lines expressing target genes

title: Lyse cells and prepare protein extracts
description: Cells were washed with PBS, scraped in lysis buffer supplemented with protease inhibitors and β-mercaptoethanol, then clarified. Extracts were processed immediately or snap-frozen for storage.
key_materials: lysis buffer (50 mM Tris–HCl pH 7.5, 0.27 M sucrose, 150 mM NaCl, 1 mM EGTA, 1 mM EDTA, 1 mM sodium orthovanadate, 10 mM sodium β-glycerophosphate, 50 mM sodium fluoride, 5 mM sodium pyrophosphate, 1% Nonidet P-40)

title: Isolate mRNAs from adult Drosophila heads
description: mRNAs were isolated from adult heads of TBPH-null alleles and wild-type flies for gene expression analysis.
goal: to analyze differences in gene expression between wild-type and TBPH-minus flies

title: Hybridize mRNAs to GeneChip Drosophila Genome Arrays
description: Isolated mRNAs were hybridized to microarrays to identify dysregulated transposons in TBPH-null flies.
goal: to identify molecules involved in neurodegeneration caused by TBPH absence

title: Confirm retrotransposon upregulation by qRT-PCR
description: Quantitative RT-PCR was used to validate microarray results showing upregulation of retrotransposons in TBPH-null heads.
key_materials: qRT-PCR primers for retrotransposons accord and gypsy

title: Detect gypsy env glycoprotein expression
description: Expression of the gypsy-encoded env glycoprotein was measured to confirm retrotransposon activity increase in TBPH mutants.
key_materials: antibodies or detection reagents for gypsy env protein
antibodies or probes for gypsy env glycoprotein

title: Genetically rescue TBPH mutants with TBPH expression
description: Expression of TBPH protein in mutant flies was used to repress activation of accord and gypsy retrotransposons.
goal: to repress retrotransposon activation in TBPH-mutant backgrounds

title: Treat TBPH-null flies with reverse transcriptase inhibitors
description: Oral administration of nucleoside and non-nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitors was performed to assess effects on locomotive defects in TBPH-null larvae.
goal: to revert locomotive defects caused by retrotransposon activation

title: Silence gypsy retrotransposon using RNAi in neurons
description: Neuronal expression of RNAi constructs targeting gypsy was used to reduce its expression and assess rescue of locomotive and synaptic defects in TBPH-null flies.
goal: to test the role of gypsy in TBPH-null phenotypes

title: Silence gypsy retrotransposon in glial cells
description: Expression of gypsy RNAi in glial cells was tested for rescue of locomotive phenotypes in TBPH-null flies.

title: Animal preparation and stereotaxic surgery
description: Male albino Wistar rats were anesthetized with chloral hydrate and positioned in a stereotaxic apparatus. Injections of vehicle, LPS, or LPS plus RU486 were made into the left substantia nigra (SN) at specified coordinates relative to bregma. Animals were assigned to different treatment groups and sacrificed at defined time points for further analysis.
goal: to administer treatments into the substantia nigra and prepare animals for downstream experiments

title: Chronic variate stress model application
description: A 9-day variate stressor paradigm was applied to stressed groups, including restraint stress and forced swimming at varying times to minimize predictability. Nonstressed animals were kept undisturbed. Body weight was measured before and after treatment as an indirect measure of HPA axis activation.
goal: to induce chronic variate stress in rats

title: Serum corticosterone measurement by ELISA
description: Blood was collected from deeply anesthetized rats via cardiac puncture. Serum corticosterone concentration was measured using an enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay according to the manufacturer's instructions.
goal: to quantify serum corticosterone levels

title: Immunohistological evaluation of brain sections
description: Coronal brain sections (20 μm) were cut and mounted. Sections were treated with hydrogen peroxide, blocked with serum, incubated with primary antibodies for 24 hours, followed by biotinylated secondary antibodies, and then incubated with ExtrAvidin–Peroxidase. Peroxidase activity was visualized using diaminobenzidine–hydrogen peroxide reaction.
goal: to detect specific proteins in brain tissue by immunohistochemistry

title: Immunohistochemical data analysis
description: Quantitative analysis was performed on defined regions of the substantia nigra using imaging software and microscopy. Areas lacking GFAP immunoreactivity were measured, and OX-6-positive cells were counted using systematic sampling with an unbiased counting frame. TH-positive neurons were estimated using a fractionator sampling design.
goal: to quantify immunohistochemical markers in brain sections

title: Immunofluorescence double-labelling
description: Brain sections were blocked with serum, incubated overnight at 4°C with combinations of primary antibodies (Iba-1 with TH or Iba-1 with IKKβ), followed by incubation with appropriate fluorescent secondary antibodies. Nuclei were counterstained with Hoechst dye. Controls included single antibody incubations. Fluorescence images were acquired by confocal microscopy.
goal: to visualize co-localization of proteins by immunofluorescence

title: Real-time RT-PCR analysis
description: The left substantia nigra was dissected 6 hours post-injection, snap-frozen, and stored. Total RNA was extracted and reverse transcribed to cDNA. Real-time PCR was performed using SYBR Green chemistry with specific primers for target genes and β-actin as reference. Amplification and melting curve analyses were conducted to confirm product specificity.
goal: to quantify mRNA expression levels of inflammatory and related genes

title: Chronic variate stress protocol
description: Animals were divided into stressed and nonstressed groups. Stressed animals underwent a 9-day variate stress paradigm including restraint in plastic tubes and forced swimming in water at controlled temperature. Stressors were applied at varying times daily to reduce predictability. Body weight was measured before and after treatment as an indirect measure of HPA axis activation.
goal: to induce chronic variate stress in rats

title: Obtain Arabidopsis accessions
description: Arabidopsis accessions and transgenic lines were obtained from various sources including stock centers and collaborators for use in the study.

title: Generate HaRxL62 expression construct
description: The ORF of HaRxL62 from the signal peptide cleavage site was cloned into pENTR/SD/D-TOPO and recombined into the Gateway destination vector under the 35S promoter to create an expression construct.
goal: to express HaRxL62 in planta

title: Transform Arabidopsis with HaRxL62 construct
description: The HaRxL62 construct was transferred into Agrobacterium and used to transform Arabidopsis Col-0 plants by floral dipping. Primary transformants were selected on BASTA-containing soil and expression was confirmed by Western blot.
goal: to generate transgenic Arabidopsis lines expressing HaRxL62

title: Select homozygous transgenic lines
description: Segregating T2 progeny were observed for 3:1 BASTA resistance, and homozygous T3 seedlings were selected based on BASTA resistance. Two independent lines were analyzed further.

title: Grow Arabidopsis for Hpa inoculation assay
description: Arabidopsis plants were grown at 22°C and 60% humidity under a 10-hour photoperiod and 14-hour dark period in controlled growth cabinets for Hpa inoculation assays.

title: Grow Arabidopsis for SA-induced PR1 expression
description: Arabidopsis plants were grown on MS medium agar plates at 22°C under a 16-hour photoperiod and 8-hour dark period in controlled growth cabinets for salicylic acid-induced PR1 expression analysis.

title: Obtain Arabidopsis Accessions and Generate Transgenic Lines
description: Arabidopsis accessions were obtained from stock centers and collaborators. A construct expressing HaRxL62 was generated by cloning the ORF into a Gateway vector under the 35S promoter, transferred into Agrobacterium, and transformed into Arabidopsis Col-0 by floral dipping. Primary transformants were selected on BASTA-containing soil and confirmed by Western blot; homozygous lines were selected in subsequent generations.
goal: to generate Arabidopsis lines expressing HaRxL62

title: Grow Arabidopsis Plants for Hpa Inoculation and SA Treatment
description: Arabidopsis plants were grown under controlled temperature, humidity, and photoperiod conditions. For Hpa inoculation, plants were grown at 22°C and 60% humidity with a 10-h photoperiod. For SA-induced PR1 expression analysis, plants were grown on MS agar plates at 22°C under a 16-h photoperiod.

title: Intranasal and Subcutaneous Vaccination of Mice
description: BALB/c mice were vaccinated twice at 6–7 week intervals with VRP-SARS-N or control VRP-GFP via intranasal (i.n.) or subcutaneous (s.c.) routes prior to SARS-CoV challenge to evaluate differences in protection and immune response localization.
goal: to evaluate the effect of vaccination route on CD4+ T cell response and protection against SARS-CoV

title: CD4+ T Cell Depletion Prior to Challenge
description: Vaccinated mice were treated systemically with CD4+ T-cell-depleting antibody 2 days or 98 days prior to SARS-CoV challenge to assess the role of memory CD4+ T cells in protection.
goal: to determine the importance of memory CD4+ T cells in protection against SARS-CoV

title: Localization of CD4+ T Cells by Dual Antibody Labeling
description: Cells were simultaneously labeled by intravenous (i.v.) and intranasal (i.n.) administration of CD90.2 and CD45 antibodies, respectively, 5–7 weeks after boosting to distinguish airway, parenchymal, and vascular CD4+ T cell populations.
goal: to discriminate anatomical localization of CD4+ T cells in respiratory tract

title: Functional Characterization of Airway CD4+ T Cells
description: Mice were treated with FTY720 to block T cell egress and with BrdU to assess proliferation, followed by analysis of cytokine expression and functional avidity of airway, parenchymal, and vascular N353-specific CD4+ T cells after SARS-CoV challenge.
goal: to evaluate proliferation, recruitment, and effector function of airway memory CD4+ T cells

title: Intranasal Depletion of Airway CD4+ T Cells
description: Airway CD4+ T cells were selectively depleted by intranasal administration of anti-CD4+ T cell antibody prior to SARS-CoV challenge to assess their role in protection.
goal: to determine the protective role of airway-localized CD4+ T cells

title: Measurement of IFN-γ Expression in Lungs
description: IFN-γ mRNA and protein expression in lungs were measured after VRP-SARS-N immunization and SARS-CoV challenge, including in vivo cytokine expression assay with BFA treatment and CD4+ T cell depletion to identify cellular sources.
goal: to assess IFN-γ production by airway CD4+ T cells after vaccination and challenge

title: Neutralization of Airway IFN-γ
description: IFN-γ was neutralized in the airway by intranasal administration of anti-IFN-γ antibody prior to and during SARS-CoV infection to evaluate its role in gene expression, pathology, survival, and virus clearance.
goal: to determine the role of airway IFN-γ in protection against SARS-CoV

title: Airway Administration of IFN-γ or TNF
description: IFN-γ or TNF was administered intranasally to mice prior to SARS-CoV challenge to test their ability to confer protection and survival.
goal: to test if airway administration of IFN-γ or TNF can protect against SARS-CoV

title: Maintain and synchronize C. elegans strains
description: Animals were maintained at 25°C using standard culture conditions and synchronized by alkaline hypochlorite treatment of gravid adults to isolate eggs.
goal: to maintain and synchronize C. elegans populations

title: Construct repair template using SapTrap
description: SapTrap was used to assemble a 30xlinker::GFP^SEC^TEV::AID degron::3xFLAG repair template (pJW1747) for knock-in into the 3′ end of the nhr-25 gene using various plasmids and PCR products.
goal: to generate a repair template for gene knock-in

title: Purify repair template plasmid
description: The pJW1747 repair template plasmid was purified using the Invitrogen PureLink HQ Mini Plasmid DNA Purification Kit with an optional wash step using guanidine-HCl and isopropanol to improve injection efficiency.
goal: to purify plasmid DNA for microinjection
key_materials: Invitrogen PureLink HQ Mini Plasmid DNA Purification Kit

title: Microinject N2 animals with plasmid mix
description: N2 animals were injected with a mix of repair template, Cas9 vector, and co-injection markers to generate knock-ins as previously described.
goal: to create gene knock-in animals

title: Verify knock-in by PCR and backcross
description: Knock-in junctions were verified by PCR using primers outside homology arms paired with primers within pJW1747, followed by five backcrosses to wild-type N2 animals.
goal: to confirm and stabilize knock-in strains

title: Excise SEC cassette by heat-shock
description: The self-excising cassette (SEC) was excised by heat-shock treatment to produce strains without the selection cassette, confirmed by PCR and sequencing.
goal: to remove selection cassette from knock-in strains

title: Prepare auxin stock solutions and plates
